British Values
As an important part of our integrated approach to Spiritual, Moral, Social & Cultural education at Tudor Academy, we promote children’s understanding of British values by embedding them across the school curriculum so that they permeate children’s learning as well as influence the values and ethos of the school.
It is our aim to ensure that children at Tudor Academy understand and actively participate in democracy, understand the difference between right and wrong, understand the rule of law, know their own personal rights and responsibilities and are mutually respectful and tolerant to those with different faiths and beliefs. At Tudor Academy we offer pupils a rigorous and challenging curriculum which encourages pupils to reflect on their role in society. These are some examples of how this is achieved:

Welcome from the Executive Head Teacher
Welcome from the Executive Head Teacher - Miz Mann
Welcome to Tudor Academy
At Tudor Academy, we are proud of the educational experiences we provide to ensure that every child can succeed. We empower our pupils to achieve their full potential academically, socially, physically, and emotionally. Our dedicated staff are committed to ensuring that every child has access to an outstanding education, enabling them to shine regardless of any barriers they may face.
At the heart of everything we do is the belief that every moment a child spends at school should be purposeful and meaningful. We provide a rich, varied, and inclusive curriculum that encourages children to develop a passion for learning across a wide range of subjects. Through a strong culture of high expectations, support, and belonging, we maximise learning opportunities and help every child achieve their full potential.
We are extremely proud of our school and would be delighted to welcome you for a visit so that you can experience our Academy in action. To arrange a tour, please contact the school office at office@tudoracademy.org.
We look forward to working in partnership and welcoming you and your family to Tudor Academy.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head Teacher
Welcome to Tudor Academy, a vibrant primary school in the heart of New Addington, Croydon. The purpose of our website is to answer the many questions you will have as a parent or carer, and to enable you to access the relevant information you will need whilst your child is a pupil at Tudor Academy. We also aim to share and celebrate daily life at Tudor and hopefully enable our website visitors to gain a better understanding of our purpose and mission.
Working in partnership with parents, children, staff, governors and our wider community is central to our vision. We aim to provide a welcoming, nurturing and stimulating environment in which all children can achieve their best – ‘Inspiring Excellence for All’.
We are committed to offering the best education for the children in our care, with inclusive classrooms at the heart of our approach. Our curriculum is designed to enhance our core values and learning behaviours of Passion, Urgency, Positivity, Aspiration and Commitment.
We have high expectations for behaviour, learning, kindness, respect and well-being. The future leaders, doctors, actors, athletes, scientists are here at Tudor! We aim to develop the whole child and know that a successful primary education is an essential component towards a smooth transition to secondary school and beyond.
Should you have any further questions, please do contact our office team using the email office@tudoracademy.org. Academy visits are warmly welcomed, so please do email or call to book an appointment.
Ms Donna Rochford Head Teacher

Religious Education
At Tudor Academy, our Religious Education (RE) curriculum is guided by our PUPAC values and the curriculum drivers of collaboration, communication, and creativity. These principles promote an environment where every child is encouraged to work together, express ideas innovatively, and develop strong communication skills. Our curriculum aims to provide rich and diverse learning experiences that equip students with the knowledge and skills to make a positive impact in a multi-religious society.
Curriculum Intent and Structure The RE curriculum at Tudor Academy is ambitious and carefully sequenced, ensuring that students' knowledge and skills grow progressively. Students explore the six major world religions: Christianity, Hinduism, Judaism, Sikhism, Buddhism, and Islam. This comprehensive approach allows students to gain an in-depth understanding of each religion's beliefs, practices, and traditions. Additionally, the curriculum covers broader concepts such as signs and symbols, special places, and the significance of pilgrimage, helping students appreciate the complexity of religious and non-religious traditions in Britain.
Learning Approach and Skills Development Students are encouraged to build on their prior knowledge through engaging discussions and critical thinking. The curriculum promotes exploration and reflection, encouraging students to ask questions and consider different perspectives. Visits to key religious sites enhance their understanding and provide real-world connections to their studies. The development of specific vocabulary related to each religion is also a key focus, helping students articulate their understanding more effectively.
Inclusivity and Broader Perspectives The RE curriculum fosters respect for diversity and promotes understanding of the multi-religious nature of society. By studying various religions and their cultural contexts, students learn to appreciate different beliefs and values. This inclusive approach supports the development of empathy and respect for others, aligning with the broader educational goals of promoting social harmony and mutual respect.
Key Features and Objectives
Progressive Knowledge Building: Students develop a thorough understanding of six major religions, with each year building on previous knowledge.
Skill Development: Focus on critical thinking, discussion, and reflection, along with the development of relevant vocabulary.
Diverse and Inclusive Content: The curriculum covers a wide range of religious beliefs and practices, fostering an appreciation of diversity and promoting social cohesion.
Through our Religious Education curriculum, Tudor Academy aims to create a learning environment that respects and understands different religious traditions, preparing students to be thoughtful and respectful members of a diverse society.

Bienvenue dans notre programme de français!
At Tudor Academy, we believe that learning the French language and culture opens doors to a world of opportunities and enriches the lives of young learners. Our primary school is dedicated to providing a comprehensive and engaging French curriculum that equips students with valuable language skills
Learning a second language is a valuable asset in today's global society, and French is a language of international significance. We understand that language is more than words; it's a bridge to diverse cultures and perspectives.
Our curriculum takes students on a captivating journey through the French-speaking world from Year 3 to Year 6. These experiences not only enhance language proficiency but also provide a deeper understanding of the diverse Francophone world.

Music
At Tudor Academy, our Music curriculum is guided by our PUPAC values and the curriculum drivers of collaboration, communication, and creativity. These principles ensure that every child is encouraged to work together, express themselves through music, and explore their creative potential. Our curriculum is designed to provide diverse and high-quality musical experiences that inspire students and help them develop a deep appreciation for music.
Curriculum Intent and Structure The Music curriculum at Tudor Academy is crafted to engage and inspire pupils, fostering a love of music and developing their talents as musicians. Our approach is inclusive, offering opportunities for all students to perform, listen to, review, and evaluate a wide range of music from different historical periods, genres, styles, and traditions. We aim to build students' confidence and creativity, helping them achieve a sense of accomplishment through music.
Students learn to sing, use their voices, create and compose music individually and collaboratively. They also have the chance to learn various musical instruments, explore music technology, and progress to higher levels of musical proficiency. The curriculum covers key musical concepts such as pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture, structure, and appropriate notations.
Learning Approach and Skills Development We implement two main programmes: Charanga and Rhythm Connection. Charanga provides structured, half-termly lessons tailored to each year group, while Rhythm Connection focuses on teaching notation, performance, and composition. Through these programmes, students explore singing, Samba drumming, glockenspiels, and more, ensuring a comprehensive musical education.
Performance and Evaluation Performance is a key component of our curriculum, with students regularly showcasing their skills in assemblies and special events, such as Christmas and end-of-year celebrations. Listening and appraising are integral parts of the programme, where students analyse core songs, identify musical elements, and discuss the emotional impact of the music. They learn to read and write music notation, developing skills in rhythm, pitch, and composition using instruments like glockenspiels and boomwhackers.
Inclusive and Cultural Awareness
Our curriculum also includes exploring the history of music across different cultures, enriching students' understanding of global musical heritage. By studying various musical traditions, from Chinese and West African music to European, Indian, and Latin American genres, students gain a broader cultural perspective and appreciation for diversity.
Key Features and Objectives
Through our Music curriculum, Tudor Academy aims to nurture students' musical abilities, confidence, and appreciation for the art, ensuring they leave with a lifelong connection to the world of music.

It was a brilliant opportunity to explore the justice system firsthand and discover the power of persuasive speaking and teamwork.

Art, Design and Technology
At Tudor Academy, we are dedicated to nurturing the artistic talents and creative spirits of young learners.
Art is more than just colours on a canvas or shapes on paper; it's a powerful means of self-expression and communication. Our art curriculum is designed to introduce students to a wide variety of artistic mediums and techniques. From painting and drawing to sculpture and digital art, we encourage students to explore their unique artistic interests and develop their skills. Pupils explore a variety of inspirational artists across their time at Tudor; they delve into their motivations and inspirations before developing their own authenticity. We encourage our pupils to express themselves in a wide range of forms and to develop the skills of fluency, experimentation and authenticity which will deepen a love for art.
We also believe that design and technology is the cornerstone of innovation and creativity. Our primary school is committed to providing an exciting and hands-on learning experience that empowers young minds to become the designers, engineers, and problem solvers of the future.
Design and technology education is essential because it equips students with the skills and knowledge needed to navigate a rapidly changing world. It fosters critical thinking, creativity, and practical problem-solving abilities.
Our curriculum encourages students to explore a wide range of design and technology concepts and projects. From crafting intricate models to designing sustainable solutions. We empower students to think creatively and make a real impact on the world around them

Accelerated Reader
Throughout the school, we have continued to develop the love for reading with the reinforcement of accelerated reader. This builds the self-independence in each of the children to read confidently and allows them to take ownership of their own reading journey. Each year group has access to Accelerated Reader, which also tracks the children’s reading age and informs the pupils of the right books to read at their specific level. The children have a variety of engaging books to read where they take quizzes on their book and move up to higher levels.

Science
At Tudor Academy, we believe that Science is the key to understanding the world around us and igniting young minds with boundless curiosity.
At Tudor Academy, our Science curriculum is guided by our PUPAC values and the curriculum drivers of collaboration, communication, and creativity. These core principles ensure that students develop not only scientific knowledge but also the skills to work together, communicate their ideas, and think creatively. Our curriculum aims to ignite curiosity and equip students with the tools to understand and engage with the world around them.
Curriculum Intent and Structure Our Science curriculum is thoughtfully designed to balance scientific content with practical skills, allowing students to explore and understand various scientific disciplines. Students develop both substantive knowledge—such as the parts of a flower or the names of planets—and disciplinary knowledge, including practical procedures and working scientifically. This comprehensive approach ensures that students build a deep understanding of scientific concepts while developing critical thinking skills.
Learning Approach and Skills Development Students are encouraged to 'think like a scientist,' engaging in activities that involve proving, disproving, and creating links between different pieces of knowledge. The curriculum covers five main areas: Human Biology, Energy, Materials, Earth Sciences, Forces, and Ecology. Each area is revisited incrementally to deepen understanding and reinforce prior learning, from Early Years through to Year 6.
Working Scientifically and Practical Application The curriculum includes a strong emphasis on working scientifically, with students participating in various enquiry types such as fair testing, observation over time, and research. They are taught to ask relevant questions, conduct experiments, observe results, and draw conclusions. This hands-on approach not only enhances their scientific understanding but also fosters an appreciation for the scientific method and its application in everyday life.
Key Features and Objectives
Through our Science curriculum, Tudor Academy aims to cultivate inquisitive and knowledgeable students who are well-prepared to understand and contribute to the world through scientific exploration and discovery.

Computing
At Tudor Academy, we empower young minds with the knowledge and skills to navigate the digital age confidently. In today's world, computing is not just a subject; it is a fundamental skill that opens doors to endless possibilities.
Curriculum Intent and Structure Our Computing curriculum aims to empower pupils as computational thinkers, providing them with the skills to understand and contribute to the technological world. The curriculum covers three main areas: Computer Science, Information Technology, and Digital Literacy. Students learn about algorithms, programming, and the secure use of the internet. They also develop practical ICT skills to engage with technology meaningfully and safely.
Learning Approach and Skills Development From Early Years through to Year 6, the curriculum progressively builds students' understanding of computing concepts. In the Early Years, children engage with technology through hands-on activities using Mini Mash and Purple Mash. As they progress, students delve into coding, digital content creation, and data management, using platforms like 2Code, 2Type, and Google Sheets. Each year group explores topics such as online safety, programming, and digital literacy, ensuring a well-rounded digital education.
Digital Literacy and Safety Digital literacy is a key focus, integrated across all year groups. Students are taught to navigate the digital world safely, understanding the importance of privacy and secure online behaviour. The curriculum includes specific lessons on online safety, helping students become responsible digital citizens.
Key Features and Objectives
Through our Computing curriculum, Tudor Academy aims to nurture confident and competent users of technology, ready to engage with and shape the digital world.

English
Underpinning all we do is a belief that every moment a child is in school is precious and so everything we do is ‘on purpose’.
Curriculum Context & Development:
In order to raise the attainment and close gaps we have chosen our approach to be Success for All. Success for All (SFA) is a reading and writing programme devised to accelerate and challenge children’s reading and writing abilities. It initially lays strong foundations in both oracy and English with Nursery and Reception children and goes on to provide systematic teaching throughout the primary years. Our provision provides a wide range of opportunities for children to explore and develop phonic knowledge and comprehension strategies; develop vocabulary and spelling; improve grammatical awareness; analyse whole texts; and develop writing in a range of genres, all whilst exposing children to a wide range of interesting, bright and diverse range of literature.

History
At Tudor Academy, our History curriculum is designed with the intent to inspire excellence for all, rooted in our core values of collaboration, creativity, and communication. We are committed to fostering a rich and inclusive learning environment that reflects our dedication to anti-racism and equipping students with the skills and knowledge to make a positive impact in the world.
Curriculum Intent and Structure The History curriculum at Tudor Academy is structured to build progressively on students' knowledge and skills. Starting from familiar contexts, students explore historical events and figures from London to broader contexts, including England, Europe, and beyond. This approach helps students understand their place in the world and the historical narratives that shape diverse cultures and identities.
Learning Approach and Skills Development Our curriculum emphasises the development of critical thinking and analytical skills. Students are encouraged to engage with historical sources, question and critique narratives, and reflect on their learning processes. Key historical skills, such as understanding chronology, exploring similarities and differences across time periods, and investigating causes and consequences, are interwoven throughout the curriculum. This comprehensive approach enables students to grasp the complexities of history and its relevance to the present day.
Inclusive and Reflective Education
We provide diverse and high-quality learning experiences that challenge students to understand and appreciate the rich tapestry of human history. By integrating discussions on various perspectives and experiences, including those of underrepresented groups, our curriculum aligns with modern educational standards and promotes an inclusive, anti-racist educational environment.
Key Features and Objectives
By engaging with our carefully curated history curriculum, Tudor Academy students develop a well-rounded, critical, and inclusive understanding of the past, preparing them for thoughtful participation in an increasingly interconnected world.
